author: jsign
content:
Thanks for clarifying. Yeah so agree then worth more eyes then. I wonder if we could also change how things work in sys-asm and re-use queue bytecode for shared system-contracts. Since, as I mention in the PR, looks like what you (or claude) did was particular tunning reg the inhibitor and hwo fee is calculated since there is no system contract call on every block to update it.

Maybe trying to reuse would end up being more complicated than a proper review from scratch; but also sharing could make the surface to review smaller. Not sure what would be the best; maybe others have an opinion.

author: jsign
content: A related thing I mention in the PR: the leanXMSS signature verifier passes all the tests generated in Ethlib which is the spec maintained by the EF cryptography team. Some days ago I added more border-cases since existing test-vectors were week, and I'm planning to FV. But I don't believe the Ethlib EVM semantics are strong enough for FV to guarantee not requiring a normal audit (but prob that's later in the process) (Edit: we still need the freeze from leanXMSS design to do any of this)

content: it's hard to reuse in this case since I wanted to add a backoff when blocks came without any prereg. Opposed to builder deposits, we really want these to be coming in *before* the fork
